title: Competitor Intelligence Profile (envelope)
description: The single source of truth for one app in a Competitive Intelligence profile set. This is a STABLE ENVELOPE, not a report: identity, a cross-cutting provenance ledger, synthesized scores, and an open `layers` map. Each intelligence domain (App Store, pricing, ad creative, SEO, sentiment, tech stack, AI visibility, ...) is a self-contained LAYER with its own schema in schema/layers/<id>.schema.json, registered in schema/layers/registry.json. A skill owns one or more layers and writes only into layers.<id>. Adding a new layer never edits this file and never invalidates existing profiles — that is the whole point of the design. The ci-appstore skill populates layers.app_store; future skills can populate the rest.

schema_version.description: Version of THIS envelope. Layers version independently via their own layer_version — so a layer can evolve without bumping the envelope.

slug.description: Stable kebab-case id; MUST equal the filename (profiles/<slug>.json). The join key across refreshes and across every CI skill. Never change it.

last_updated.description: ISO date of the most recent write to this profile by any skill.

is_baseline.description: True only for your own app's profile (the baseline), which anchors every comparison. Default false.

vendor.description: Parent company / publisher of the app.

app_store_slug.description: The apps.shopify.com/<slug> path — sometimes reveals keyword strategy (e.g. a category keyword in the handle).

layers.description: The extensibility point. Keys are layer ids from schema/layers/registry.json (e.g. 'app_store', 'pricing', 'ad_creative'). Each value is a layer object that MUST carry a `meta` block (validated here) plus its own domain fields (validated against that layer's schema by scripts/validate_profiles.py). An unknown/planned layer is simply absent — never a null placeholder, never a schema change.

meta.description: Common header every layer carries, so the platform can reason about any layer uniformly (who wrote it, when, how fresh) without knowing its domain.

layer_id.description: Must match the key in `layers` and an entry in registry.json.

collected_by.description: Skill that owns this layer, e.g. 'ci-appstore'.

layer_version.description: Version of the layer schema this data conforms to.

status.description: populated = fully collected; partial = some fields pending; stale = past the refresh horizon, re-collect before trusting.

layers_populated.description: Denormalized list of layer ids present in `layers`, for cheap discovery ('which competitors have ad_creative data?') without opening every profile. Keep in sync with the keys of `layers`.

scores.description: Cross-cutting analyst scores synthesized from whatever layers are present (1–5). Kept in the envelope, not a layer, because they are a view ACROSS layers. Weighted values are computed by scripts, not hand-entered, so weights stay consistent across competitors. Extend with new named views as more layers land.

claims.description: Unified provenance ledger for the WHOLE profile — every load-bearing fact from every layer, each tagged with its `layer`. This is what makes the platform trustworthy: on refresh, unchanged claims are trusted, 'stale' claims re-fetched, 'refuted' claims kept so they can't creep back in. One ledger (not per-layer) so cross-layer facts and de-duplication stay simple.

layer.description: Layer id this claim supports, or null for envelope-level facts (identity, scores).

field.description: Dotted path the claim backs, e.g. 'layers.app_store.pricing.tiers[0].monthly_usd'.

statement.description: The fact in one sentence, as a human would read it.

source_type.description: Free-form but prefer a stable vocabulary, e.g. 'app_store_listing', 'app_store_reviews', 'vendor_site', 'wayback', 'meta_ad_library', 'g2', 'analyst_inference'.

verification.description: verified = independently corroborated; unverified = single-source, believed true; refuted = checked and false (kept deliberately); stale = past the refresh horizon.

refresh_history.description: Append one entry each time any layer is re-collected, so change-over-time is auditable without a separate log.

notes.description: What materially changed since the prior snapshot (price move, review jump, new complaint theme).
